stack_and_runtime_constraints: TypeScript backend with AWS CDK and Node.js 20 lambdas.
Current runtime shape is EventBridge Scheduler -> Producer Lambda -> SQS FIFO -> Orchestrator Lambda -> Step Functions -> Consumer Lambda.
Pending records, idempotency records, and results are persisted in DynamoDB.
architecture_shape: Phase 2 already introduced retries, idempotency, and lifecycle closure in Step Functions.
Phase 3 already introduced dispatch-slot partitioning and 288 distributed schedules.
The current repository still has critical gaps in end-to-end provider serialization, retry specificity, failure auditability, and productive slot materialization.
likely_touched_modules: CDK infrastructure for queue consumption and state machine topology.
Consumer error contract and state machine failure handling.
Pending-record write path and dispatch-slot metadata ownership.
Final architecture documentation and traceability artifacts.
test_setup_available: Jest unit tests for CDK, consumer, orchestrator, and producer modules.
Build pipeline through TypeScript project references.
Existing phase 2 and phase 3 validation docs for AWS proof paths.

product_scope.problem_statement: The repository already demonstrates a scalable serverless architecture, but it still contains critical behavioral gaps that make the challenge answer incomplete: same-provider concurrency can still leak, terminal errors can still be retried, failure persistence loses the real provider status code, distributed dispatch depends on pre-seeded routing metadata, and the final architecture lacks a reviewer-ready documentation package.
product_scope.goal: Close the final architecture gaps so the solution becomes behaviorally correct, operationally defendable, and document-complete for the Tapi technical challenge.
success_outcomes: A single provider never receives concurrent executions for the same ordered queue stream.
Retry behavior clearly distinguishes transient from terminal failures.
Persisted failure records preserve the real provider status code for audit.
New pending records receive productive dispatch-slot metadata automatically.
The repository includes a clear architecture document and requirement-to-solution traceability.

in_scope: End-to-end same-provider serialization through the runtime path that starts at SQS FIFO and ends after provider execution completes.
Functional distinction between retryable and non-retryable provider failures.
Accurate persistence of provider failure outcomes for auditability.
Productive ownership of dispatch-slot routing metadata at pending-record creation time.
Reviewer-facing architecture documentation and traceability artifacts.
out_of_scope: Business-rule changes to provider payloads or endpoint semantics.
Cost optimization beyond what is necessary to make the architecture technically defendable.
A broader rewrite of producer/consumer business contracts unrelated to the five identified issues.

actors.name: Scheduler Layer
actors.description: Starts the distributed daily dispatch windows.

actors.name: Dispatch Flow
actors.description: Selects pending work and publishes ordered provider messages.

actors.name: Ordered Execution Boundary
actors.description: Owns the guarantee that same-provider work remains serialized until execution truly finishes.

actors.name: Operational Workflow
actors.description: Owns retries, lifecycle transitions, and final persistence.

actors.name: Technical Reviewer
actors.description: Evaluates whether the final repository is correct, scalable, and clearly documented.

user_journeys.name: Serialized provider execution remains intact end to end
steps: Two or more work items for the same provider enter the ordered queue.
The runtime consumes the first work item and starts the provider execution flow.
The next work item for that same provider does not progress into effective provider execution until the previous one is fully closed.
Different providers may continue progressing independently.

user_journeys.name: Transient and terminal failures follow different operational paths
steps: The system classifies the failure as transient or terminal.
Transient failures may be retried according to policy.
Terminal failures skip retries and close immediately through a final failure path.

user_journeys.name: Failure audit preserves the real provider outcome
steps: A provider responds with a failure status code.
The execution flow captures the real provider status code and error context.
The final persisted result reflects that real status code rather than a synthetic placeholder.

user_journeys.name: New pending records become dispatchable without manual seeding
steps: A new pending record is created for a scheduled date.
The system assigns dispatch-slot routing metadata as part of the productive write path.
The distributed dispatch flow can later select that record by slot without requiring a separate manual enrichment step.

user_journeys.name: A reviewer can defend the final architecture
steps: A reviewer inspects the repository after the remediation.
They find a clear architecture document and a requirement-to-solution narrative.
They can explain how scale, ordering, retries, persistence, and documentation now align with the challenge.

use_cases.title: Prevent same-provider concurrency leakage
use_cases.description: The system must preserve one-at-a-time execution per provider until the provider call is truly completed.

use_cases.title: Retry only transient failures
use_cases.description: The system must reattempt only failures that are expected to succeed later.

use_cases.title: Persist accurate terminal and exhausted failure evidence
use_cases.description: The system must store the real provider status code and failure context for final audit.

use_cases.title: Generate productive dispatch-slot metadata
use_cases.description: The system must automatically assign distributed routing metadata when a pending record is created.

use_cases.title: Deliver reviewer-ready final architecture documentation
use_cases.description: The repository must expose a clear architectural explanation and traceability from challenge requirements to solution behavior.

business_rules.rule: The same provider must never receive concurrent effective executions from the ordered work stream.
Different providers may continue progressing in parallel.
Terminal provider failures must not be retried.
Transient provider failures may be retried according to policy.
Final persisted failure evidence must preserve the real provider status code.
Distributed dispatch metadata must be generated by the productive system, not only by test seeds.
The final repository must include explicit architecture documentation suitable for technical evaluation.

functional_requirements.title: End-to-end provider serialization
functional_requirements.statement: The runtime must keep same-provider ordered work serialized until the provider execution flow has fully completed.

functional_requirements.title: Retry specificity
functional_requirements.statement: The workflow must retry transient failures and skip retries for terminal failures.

functional_requirements.title: Accurate failure auditability
functional_requirements.statement: The final persisted failure result must include the real provider status code and failure category.

functional_requirements.title: Productive slot materialization
functional_requirements.statement: The system must assign dispatch-slot routing fields when pending records are created or written into productive storage.

functional_requirements.title: Architecture documentation completeness
functional_requirements.statement: The repository must provide a clear architecture diagram and a requirement-to-solution traceability narrative.

functional_requirements.title: Behavior preservation outside the fixes
functional_requirements.statement: The remediation must preserve the existing daily scheduling, distributed dispatch shape, and downstream result persistence responsibilities unless a change is necessary to resolve one of the identified critical issues.

interaction_expectations.expectation: A reviewer should be able to explain the concurrency guarantee without relying on hidden implementation assumptions.
Operational failure outcomes should be understandable from persisted data alone.
The remediation should feel like a completion of the current architecture, not a contradictory redesign.

acceptance_criteria.given: Two work items belong to the same provider
acceptance_criteria.when: The runtime processes them from the ordered queue
acceptance_criteria.then: The second work item does not reach effective provider execution until the first one has fully closed.

acceptance_criteria.given: A provider call fails with a terminal business error
acceptance_criteria.then: The execution skips retries and closes directly through the terminal failure path.

acceptance_criteria.given: A provider call fails with a transient error
acceptance_criteria.then: The execution retries according to the defined transient retry policy before final closure.

acceptance_criteria.given: A provider returns a specific failure status code such as 401, 403, 429, 502, or 503
acceptance_criteria.when: The final failure result is persisted
acceptance_criteria.then: The stored result preserves that real status code rather than replacing it with a fixed placeholder.

acceptance_criteria.given: A new pending record is created through the productive write path
acceptance_criteria.then: It already contains the dispatch-slot routing metadata needed for distributed selection.

acceptance_criteria.when: They inspect the final architecture documentation
acceptance_criteria.then: They can trace the challenge requirements to the implemented runtime behaviors and architectural decisions.

assumptions: The current producer contract and distributed daily scheduling model remain valid and should be preserved where possible.
The remediation can replace the current queue-to-workflow bridge if that is necessary to guarantee same-provider serialization.
The final documentation artifact belongs in the repository root as a reviewer-facing deliverable.
Existing phase 2 and phase 3 guarantees remain the baseline and are being corrected or completed rather than discarded.

open_questions.question: Which runtime bridge replaces the current orchestrator path to preserve end-to-end ordered execution?
open_questions.resolved_as: EventBridge Pipes with synchronous invocation into an Express Step Functions workflow.

open_questions.question: Where should dispatch-slot routing metadata become authoritative?
